files.why: Server shapes (zod schemas) are the boundary that mirrors the API: rename the DTO keys and nest invoiceLineDtoSchema one level deeper (e.g. a wrapper object) to match the new response.
toInvoice/toInvoiceDto read/write the renamed DTO fields and the deeper line-items path; updating only the mapper keeps core entities unchanged (the whole point of this layer).
MSW seed data is served in raw server shape and validated by invoiceDtoSchema.parse, so it must adopt the new field names and line nesting or every fetch throws.
Its InvoiceDto fixture uses the old flat, old-named shape; update it to the new keys/nesting so the mapping and round-trip assertions still exercise a schema-valid DTO.

uncertain: Whether the API change is a pure rename (absorbed entirely by data/, core untouched) or whether a renamed field actually carries new meaning — if so, core/types.ts, core/rules.ts, and ui components could also need changes. I assumed a pure rename per the README's stability-layer model.
mocks.ts: I assumed the frontend still owns MSW seed fixtures that must track the new shape; if the team has a shared/generated contract or the mock is meant to lag behind, placement could differ.

Exact nesting target for 'one level deeper' (a new wrapper key on the invoice vs. lines becoming { items: [...] } vs. a nested container object) — the shape drives the precise dto.ts/mappers.ts edits.
questions: What is the exact old->new field-name mapping, and which fields are affected (invoice level, line level, or both)?
What is the precise new nesting for line items — the new key name(s) and structure the array now lives under?
Do value encodings also change (still snake_case, money-as-strings, ISO dates, integer status enum) or only names/nesting?
Is this a hard cutover, or must the client temporarily accept both old and new shapes during backend rollout (would require dual-parsing logic in data/)?
Do all invoice endpoints share the new shape (list /api/invoices, detail /api/invoices/:id, and the void PATCH response), or only some?
